resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. platform_and_boundaries §1 (also §6d) line 73: harm: I verified the judge's citations. They are accurate, but they don't show a blocking harm.

What checks out:
- training-architecture.md L88 and L90 say `module-1/personal-brand-generation.md` stays scoped to Module 1, and Module 2 starts with zero root rules.
- getting-going.md L107 says the file is "not an M2 input".
- L70 says to start Module 2 fresh.
- The line at L73 came from commit 70bad713, a solo-learner wording pass. It was not a deliberate technical claim.

Why it still fails:
- (a) Harm. Line 73 says the rules file "carries what you learned into the next session". It does not say the file auto-loads or that Module 2 will read it. The file does persist on disk. The exercise body frames it the same way at exercises/personal-site-with-guardrails.md L7: "package what you learned for the next session". The `-cb` variant of the exercise calls it "a portable agent guideline I could invoke on the next personal-brand task" and says "the file is the thing that travels". So the line restates the exercise's own promise. A student who points a later session at the file gets exactly what the line says. A student whose Module 2 session doesn't see it loses nothing. Module 2 supplies its context through pasted prompts, and the Debrief builds the root file from scratch. The cost is a moment of mild confusion on a closing "Next" slide, not a wrong action.
- (b) Restatement. The architecture "scoped to module-1/" rule is about auto-load scope. The judge treats that as proof that no carry exists. Disk persistence and portability are untouched by it.
- (c) and (d) Cost of the fix. The "Next" slide is a deliberate bridge, set up by L70's "start fresh" and the exercise's "next session" framing. The proposed rewrite, "Module 2 starts fresh and grows a memory", is arguably cleaner. But the original is not false, and the fix is wording polish rather than a correction.
- Rule fit. check_platform_and_boundaries §1 concerns surface or profile claims outside a training's runtime contract. §6d concerns what auto-loads. Line 73 makes neither claim. At most this is an ambiguity nit in "already carries", not a BLOCKING platform-contract violation.
